races.notes: Per AP (Oct 2), SLF 'will make a seven-figure advertising buy in Kansas'. NC Newsline, citing Semafor, says SLF is shifting North Carolina money to Kansas (https://www.newsfromthestates.com/node/430525). Hamilton raised $3.66M from 16,000 people in his first 62 days (Kansas Reflector, https://kansasreflector.com/?p=60968) and $1.01M from 6,700 people in his first week (Kansas Reflector, May 4, https://kansasreflector.com/?p=59761). Libertarian David C. Graham is also on the ballot. AdImpact reservations for the month from ~Oct 2 (AP): pro-Marshall about $11.0M (SLF ~$8.2M, campaign $2.3M, others $0.5M) vs pro-Hamilton about $1.15M (campaign $590K, outside ~$556K); CBS puts SLF's Kansas reservation at $9.8M. Senate Majority PAC was 'actively thinking' about whether to wade into Kansas, and Schumer has included Kansas in private donor pitches (Politico, Oct 2). In August an unnamed super PAC ran ads quoting a Hamilton sermon on the beef industry; a Hamilton ad said 'Maybe Marshall hasn't noticed farm bankruptcy is piling up on his watch.' (KWCH, https://www.kwch.com/2026/08/19/kansas-senate-race-tightens-hamilton-marshall-trade-attacks/).

ads.transcript: [Jody S.:] I have a story to tell about our senator, Pete Ricketts. On April 30, 1993, John Arias broke into my home, tied me up with parachute cord and violently raped me. My children heard everything that happened. He was caught, pled guilty and went to prison. He said I should watch my back for the rest of my life. Pete Ricketts cast the deciding vote to pardon this man. [Female voice, pardon board audio:] Governor Ricketts. [Ricketts, pardon board audio:] Yes. But with that, you've got your pardon. [Jody S.:] That pardon brought back all the nightmares. I found out just totally by accident. I thought impossible that anyone would make that decision without contacting the victim. Because of Pete Ricketts, my attacker is now allowed to own a gun and had his name removed from the sex offender registry. I have no idea why Senator Ricketts chose my rapist over me. [Male voice:] Nebraska Values PAC is responsible for the content of this advertising.
on_screen_sources: 1990s newspaper headlines about the case (per NYT)

races.notes: No Democrat on the ballot: the Nebraska Examiner (Jul 28) calls Cindy Burbank the 'former Democratic nominee, removed from the ballot'. The shared senate.json, without a URL, says she withdrew Jul 17 and the party endorsed Osborn. Ricketts-linked committees in Q2: Ricketts Victory Committee (JFC) raised $566,137 and American Excellence PAC raised $154,637; these are not independent expenditures. 2024 context, not 2026: the Ricketts campaign claimed 'Democrat Super PACs spent more than $20 million' to elect Osborn in 2024, and the DSCC gave late help; in Oct 2025 Nebraska Democrats said they were not recruiting a Senate candidate (Nebraska Examiner, https://www.newsfromthestates.com/node/370213). In Q1 2026 Osborn outraised Ricketts, $1.2M to $1.0M (https://nebraskaexaminer.com/?p=40405). 2026 general: Osborn acknowledged that some dark-money-funded ads support his campaign but said he doesn't stand by ads that lack his approval; Ricketts' campaign ads use leaked recordings of Osborn, which Osborn called a 'joke' that takes his words out of context (Nebraska Examiner, Sep 1 and Sep 10: https://www.newsfromthestates.com/node/425405 ; https://www.newsfromthestates.com/node/427058). Osborn said at the Sep 1 debate that he has about 71,000 individual donors averaging about $40.
